rationale: No story/spec artifact was supplied for this standalone review, so acceptance did not run and this is a genuine no-spec round (confidence capped at low); 4 patch-grade defects survived triage against the real source (credential-presence check inconsistency, an unhandled StaleDataError race, a lost npx remediation hint on redisplay, and a response-model change that breaks two existing create_user_setting tests). 0 findings deferred. 8 lens-reported candidates were verified against source and dismissed as false positives or already-guarded/intentional (re-exported CredentialTypes enum identity, the documented marketplace=True access rule, a stale alias display field, a missing DB check constraint, an unreachable category=None path, dual last_test_message semantics that match an explicit in-code design comment, the documented last-write-wins test-result persistence, and MCPConfigListResponse which already reuses MCPConfigResponse and so already carries the last_test_* fields).

findings.title: create_user_setting AttributeError on saved.id_
findings.problem: create_user_setting now does `saved = SettingsService.create_setting(...)` then `CreateSettingResponse(message=..., id=saved.id_)`. Two pre-existing tests (test_create_user_setting_success and test_create_user_setting_with_project_access_check in tests/codemie/rest_api/routers/test_user_settings_crud.py) mock SettingsService.create_setting to return None and assert HTTP 200, which the diff did not update.
findings.impact: Those tests will now fail: `None.id_` raises AttributeError, caught by the surrounding `except Exception` and turned into an HTTP 422 instead of the expected 200 with `{"message": "Specified credentials saved"}`. Production is unaffected (the real SettingsService.create_setting always returns a Settings object), but the suite breaks on the next run.
findings.recommendation: Update the two tests' `create_setting` mocks to return an object exposing `id_` (or a real-shaped stub), and update the asserted response body to include the new `id` field.

findings.title: GET redisplay loses npx-specific hint
findings.problem: build_hint_for_category_value() reconstructs a hint for a persisted error_category using a dummy `MCPServerDetails(name="", enabled=True)`, which has no `command`. `_build_hint_for_category`'s `is_npx = command == "npx"` check is therefore always False on this path, so a persisted CONNECTION_CLOSED category whose original failure actually came from an npx server never gets the detailed npx remediation hint.
findings.impact: An admin who re-fetches the config later (GET) only sees the generic 'check the server process' hint instead of the specific npx guidance they got on the original POST /test, degrading the error-messaging feature this change exists to add.
findings.recommendation: Persist the originating command (or an `is_npx` flag) alongside `error_category` in MCPTestDetail, and pass it into the dummy MCPServerDetails reconstruction so the npx-specific hint can be regenerated on later reads.

findings.title: Inconsistent truthiness in required-env-var check
findings.problem: `_missing_required_env_vars` builds its `provided` set with two different truthiness rules: `config.env` literals only count when `if v` (truthy), but `setting.credential_values` keys are added unconditionally (`{cred.key for cred in setting.credential_values or []}`), regardless of whether the value is empty/blank.
findings.impact: An integration credential with an empty value is wrongly treated as satisfying a required var, letting the test proceed to actually contact the server instead of returning the clear 'Missing required credentials' message; conversely, a deliberate empty-string override in config.env is wrongly treated as missing, blocking the test with a misleading error even though the value was intentionally set.
findings.recommendation: Apply the same presence rule to both sources — e.g. treat a key as provided only when its value is not None/blank in both config.env and credential_values, or document why the two sources intentionally use different rules.

findings.title: Unhandled StaleDataError on concurrent config delete
findings.problem: `_persist_test_result` re-fetches the config to guard against stale overwrites, but if the config is deleted between that re-fetch (line 471) and the subsequent `mcp_config.update(touch_timestamp=False)` call (line 483), the base model's update() raises StaleDataError, which is not caught here.
findings.impact: A client that deletes a config while a slow test for the same config is in flight gets an unhandled exception propagating as an HTTP 500 instead of the expected 404 'MCP configuration not found' response.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the update() call in a try/except StaleDataError and raise cls._not_found(config_id), matching the pattern already used for the initial find_by_id check.
